pos.personaBrief: Toque toque side that subdued rivals with possession (Perfil 442, RCN 'tocar y tocar'), but also content to sit back and counter in the 5-0 (FourFourTwo, Planet Football); possession is the identity, not dogma.

pro.personaBrief: Centre-backs and midfielders circulate the ball short to build out (La Grinta), with long balls only when attackers have a clear advantage (RCN).

est.personaBrief: Zonal order without the ball but fluid, close combinations with Valderrama and diagonal runs by the forwards, midfielders dropping in turn (La Grinta, RCN).

lar.personaBrief: 4-4-2 near diamond with no true wingers; play runs through Valderrama centrally, with full-backs attacking the flanks on recovery (La Grinta, Trivela).

blo.personaBrief: Advanced marking and high press per FourFourTwo and Trivela, though La Grinta says pressing came in sequences by context and they sat back in the 5-0 second half.

mar.personaBrief: Maturana's zonal marking with a back four, a pioneer of zonal defence in South America (RCN, El Pais, La Grinta).

pla.personaBrief: Maturana imposed his own toque model and kept it; Colombia played the same way regardless of opponent, with Dutch influence and the aim of expressing the country's identity (statedView).

res.personaBrief: Maturana wanted to play football and leave a footprint rather than neutralise opponents (Coaches' Voice), valuing style; the 5-0 showed he also took a draw that qualified.

sis.personaBrief: Eleven players who produce play inside a zonal order, with Valderrama as free creative hub and Rincon loose without defensive obligations (Trivela, RCN).

jog.personaBrief: Squad of high technical quality, everyone willing to pass short or long (La Grinta), built around the classic number 10 Valderrama.

bas.personaBrief: Squad rooted in Atletico Nacional so it could train daily (Coaches' Voice), with some young players like Cordoba and Higuita; neither a youth nor a veteran dogma.

lid.personaBrief: Maturana ringfenced the environment, protected players after elimination and favoured a happy group and dialogue (Coaches' Voice, FourFourTwo).
